summary.en: Protesters in India’s Cockroach movement are bypassing internet blackouts with Bluetooth and defying a ban on a protest site, while leaders of the movement have been jailed. In Manipur, a suspected mass food poisoning has hospitalized dozens of BSF personnel, a woman was killed and two civilians missing after an ambush in Kamjong, and the Makui Village Authority condemned firing and demanded security intervention. The state lost Rs 1,200 crore in GST revenue amid the ethnic unrest. A prayer for peace was called for as new violence broke out. 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Protestere i Indias Cockroach-bevegelse omgår internettblackouts med Bluetooth og trosser et forbud mot et proteststed, mens ledere i bevegelsen er fengslet. I Manipur har en mistenkt masseforgiftning av mat innlagt dusinvis av BSF-personell på sykehus, en kvinne ble drept og to sivile savnet etter et bakholdsangrep i Kamjong, og Makui Village Authority fordømte skytingen og krevde sikkerhetsintervensjon. Staten mistet 1 200 crore rupee i GST-inntekter på grunn av den etniske uroen. En bønn om fred ble uttalt da ny vold brøt ut. 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
